modelResponse.episodeSummary: Margaret Sullivan, 74F, Torsades de Pointes, critical, hypotensive
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Sinusoidal amplitude modulation with axis twisting
preEventNote: Baseline ECG 6 min prior: sinus 62, marked QT prolongation QTc 618 ms, prominent U waves
modelResponse.mechanism: Delayed afterdepolarization (EAD) triggered activity due to prolonged repolarization

rejectedAlternatives.why: The specific morphology described ('Sinusoidal amplitude modulation with axis twisting') and the baseline ECG finding of marked QT prolongation strongly point towards Torsades de Pointes rather than other forms of polymorphic VT.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Atrial Fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
rejectedAlternatives.why: The ECG morphology is not consistent with AFib; the rhythm is polymorphic and twisting, not irregularly irregular narrow complex tachycardia.
While the patient is hypotensive, there is no fever (temperatureC: 36.7) or other clear signs of sepsis in the provided data. The primary driver is the ECG findings and electrolyte abnormalities.

recommendedActions: Administer Potassium Chloride 20 mEq IV (monitor closely)
Prepare for synchronized cardioversion if hemodynamically unstable or refractory to magnesium
Correct dehydration with IV fluids (e.g., Normal Saline)
uncertainty: Exact timing and dose of azithromycin administration.
Presence of other QT-prolonging medications not listed.
